feedback: Decision: approve. This candidate changes one field group from the best raced design (iteration 5, score 81.82): base_speed 1.2 to 1.0. Geometry, kp 4.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.30, sensor weights and line_loss search_left are unchanged. The evidence supports the test. Oval max_error has been 0.0605 to 0.0626 across iterations 3 to 5, just over the 0.06 m off-track limit, and iteration 5 showed the largest oval gain from the speed drop (progress 0.137 to 0.318). Oval line-loss events fell to 0.15 with search_left. On s-bend and slalom, line_loss_events stayed at 1 under every recovery direction tried, and progress barely moved, so speed is not their limiting factor. Steering oscillation on the oval was 0.183 in iteration 5, above the 0.15 guide. We are in mid-run with 5 iterations left, and this candidate is valid and isolates speed, so racing it gives the most useful telemetry. Do not assume it beats iteration 5 until the race shows it. Read the next race as follows. (a) If oval progress stays at or above 0.318 and oval max_error falls below 0.06, keep base_speed 1.0. (b) If oval progress falls well below 0.318, speed 1.0 is too slow; return to 1.1 or 1.2 and test a different lever. (c) If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.15 while max_error is still at or above 0.06, reduce kd to about 0.20 before changing kp. (d) If s-bend or slalom still show one line-loss event, change the sensor layout (a wider spread or a forward fifth sensor) rather than the recovery direction.
requested_changes: If oval progress falls below 0.318 at base_speed 1.0 (iteration 5 value at 1.2), set base_speed to about 1.1 and keep kd 0.30 and search_left, so speed is tuned between 1.0 and 1.2 without changing steering.

If oval max_error stays at or above 0.06 with steering_oscillation above 0.15 at base_speed 1.0, reduce controller.kd from 0.30 to about 0.20 with all other fields fixed. Evidence: iteration 5 oval oscillation was 0.183 at kd 0.30, and iteration 1 showed kd 0.30 raised oscillation above 0.15.

If s-bend or slalom line_loss_events stay at 1 after this race, change the sensor layout (for example a fifth sensor forward at y 0.06, or a wider spread) with the speed and recovery direction held fixed. Evidence: line_loss stayed at 1 with last_direction (iterations 0 to 3) and search_right (iteration 4) on those tracks.
